note: Literature and preclinical models support that inner retinal bipolar cell dysfunction and synaptic transmission failure cause electronegative ERGs in early CLN3 disease prior to late outer retinal loss.

evidence.text: In a Cln3-deficient mouse model, decline in inner retinal function was caused by rod bipolar cell death, and inner retina-targeted AAV therapy rescued retinal function whereas photoreceptor-targeted therapy failed, supporting inner retinal/bipolar involvement prior to late photoreceptor loss.

source.title: Gene therapy targeting the inner retina rescues the retinal phenotype in a mouse model of CLN3 Batten disease
source.quote: treatment of photoreceptors, which are lost in patients at late disease stages, was not therapeutic in Cln3Δex7/8 mice, underlining the notion that CLN3 disease is primarily a disease of the inner retina with secondary changes in the outer retina.

evidence.text: All five confirmed CLN3 patients presenting early (median age 6.2 years) exhibited an electronegative ERG accompanying early maculopathy.

source.title: Early recognition of CLN3 disease facilitated by visual electrophysiology and multimodal imaging
source.quote: Electronegative ERGs were identified in all patients.
